neighbours.label: ' run' in 'run the risk' and ' stresses' in 'stresses that': verbs that raise a warning or emphasis; promotes ' the'. Plain ' run' and neutral reporting verbs in the same frames stay quiet. A list, not shown as one pattern
fire: If you skip the test, you run the risk of failure.
Move too fast and you run the danger of a fall.
The institute stresses that children need sleep.
The report stresses how much the town has changed.
Investors run the risk of losing it all.
The guide stresses that boots must fit.
By waiting, we run the risk of missing the train.
Our coach stresses that effort matters most.
quiet: If you skip the test, you run home early.
Move too fast and you run past the fall.
The institute says that children need sleep.
The report shows how much the town has changed.
Investors run the firm and own it all.
The guide says that boots must fit.
By waiting, we saw the train go by.
Our coach thinks that effort matters most.
